Withings' service has support to notify an app when data changes (webhooks). In order to support webhooks, substantial changes were required to the entire integration. review_comments: Don't register this until you know you're authenticated ?
Doesn't this depend on if the webhook is used?

This does not depend on if the webhook is used.
Data updates are performed by the data manager which polls for new data every 30min. If webhooks are enabled, withings will tell HA that data has changed (not what changed). This triggers data manager to run another update earlier than usual.
After processing data, data manager will trigger HA to update entities.
The only exception for data collection is for in/out of bed detection. The webhook is the only medium for receiving this data and is handled as a special case in the data manager's `async_webhook_data_updated` method. At any rate, the data manager still processes the data and tell HA to update the necessary entities.

The previous version of this component struggled with dozens of polling sensors triggering a data manager update. The problem was only 2 API calls were needed to gather all the data and a lot of code was used to throttle/cache results. Additionally, this older model simply could not support webhooks.

I think that Withings should try not to add all possible data by default, but disable some entiteis by deafult that might be less important. The user can then enable them later. This can be controlled by returning `False` from `Entity.entity_registry_enabled_default`. Do you think that the weight/temperature measurement breakdown by type should be disabled by default?

This makes sense. Half of the entities do not provide relatively immediate results and can be disabled.
I played around with disabling these by default but I could not get their states to be registered after enabling them. It looks like since the entity is disabled by default, the entity is never added to hass and thus has no place for states. Setting `disabled_by = None` for the `EntityEntry` in the `EntityRegistry` has no effect as it looks like the `async_add_entities` is the only entrypoint for getting entities added to hass.
Home Assistant will reload your config entry (unload, then load again) to re-enable entities.
What's the preferred method of testing this behavior? Just making reload for the config entry?
Patch it so that it returns `True` from `Entity.entity_registry_enabled_default`
